## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The new `--exclude` flag does not take its default from an `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE` environment variable, which the project's cli-flags policy requires for every new flag under `cli/`. Apart from that, the exclusion logic and its tests are consistent with the stated behaviour.

## Changes
The pull request adds a repeatable `--exclude GLOB` option that drops files from the archive when their base name matches any of the given patterns, and logs each skipped file. It also documents the flag in `docs/flags.md` and adds parser, `collect` and end-to-end tests.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- cli/main.py:17 — correctness — Read the --exclude default from ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE — When CI sets `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE=*.log` and runs `archive src`, nothing is excluded, because the parser sets `default=[]` and never reads the environment. Policy `.claude/skills/cli-flags/SKILL.md:11` says: "Every command-line flag added under `cli/` from now on must also take its default from an `ARCHIVE_<NAME>` environment variable". — CI jobs that pass options through the environment cannot use `--exclude`, so excluded files still end up in their archives. — Fix: Parse `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE` into a fresh list for `default=`, using a documented separator for multiple globs; note that `action="append"` adds command-line patterns to that default instead of replacing it, then cover the variable in `test_exclude_defaults_to_nothing` or a sibling test.
